**Zuzana Čaputová** ( Slovak pronunciation: [ˈzuzana ˈtʂaputɔʋaː]; [née](Birth_name#Maiden_and_married_names "Birth name") **Strapáková**; born 21 June 1973) is a Slovak politician, lawyer and environmental activist. She is the fifth [president of Slovakia](President_of_Slovakia "President of Slovakia"), a position she has held since 15 June 2019. Čaputová is the first woman to hold the presidency, as well as the youngest president in the history of Slovakia, elected at the age of 45.[[2]](Zuzana_%C4%8Caputov%C3%A1#cite_note-nyt-won-2)

Čaputová first became known by prevailing in a decade-long struggle against the situating of a toxic landfill in her hometown of <Pezinok>. For this, Čaputová was awarded the 2016 [Goldman Environmental Prize](Goldman_Environmental_Prize "Goldman Environmental Prize"). She won the [2019 Slovak presidential election](2019_Slovak_presidential_election "2019 Slovak presidential election") with 58% of the vote in the run-off.

## Early life and education

Zuzana Čaputová was born into a working-class family in <Bratislava>.[[3]](Zuzana_%C4%8Caputov%C3%A1#cite_note-fp-candidate-3)[[4]](Zuzana_%C4%8Caputov%C3%A1#cite_note-afp-won-4) She grew up in the nearby town of <Pezinok>,[[4]](Zuzana_%C4%8Caputov%C3%A1#cite_note-afp-won-4) in what was <Czechoslovakia> for the first two decades of her life. She has described her upbringing as having occurred within "an open-minded house".[[3]](Zuzana_%C4%8Caputov%C3%A1#cite_note-fp-candidate-3)

She studied at the [Comenius University](Comenius_University "Comenius University") Faculty of Law in Bratislava,[[4]](Zuzana_%C4%8Caputov%C3%A1#cite_note-afp-won-4) graduating in 1996.[[5]](Zuzana_%C4%8Caputov%C3%A1#cite_note-tasr-bio-5) Between 1998 and 1999 she completed the training cycle "General Management – Management of Change" and in 1999 the ARK – Mediation course, accredited by the Ministry of Education of Slovakia.[[6]](Zuzana_%C4%8Caputov%C3%A1#cite_note-6)

## Early career

After concluding her education, Čaputová worked in the local government of <Pezinok>, first as an assistant in the legal department, and later as a deputy to the town mayor.[[7]](Zuzana_%C4%8Caputov%C3%A1#cite_note-TASR-7)

She later moved into the non-profit sector at the [Open Society Foundations](Open_Society_Foundations "Open Society Foundations"), where she handled public administration and the issue of abused and exploited children. Subsequently, she worked as a project manager at the civic association EQ Klub on local community development.[[8]](Zuzana_%C4%8Caputov%C3%A1#cite_note-8)

Between 2001 and 2017, Čaputová worked with *Via Iuris*, a civic organization, as a lawyer (since 2010),[[7]](Zuzana_%C4%8Caputov%C3%A1#cite_note-TASR-7) and with <Greenpeace> on campaign planning.[[9]](Zuzana_%C4%8Caputov%C3%A1#cite_note-9) In Pezinok, for more than ten years, she was at the forefront of a public campaign against the authorization of another landfill that would aggravate pollution of the soil, air, and water in the city and its surrounding areas. **Katerina Sakellaropoulou** ([Greek](Greek_language "Greek language"): Κατερίνα Σακελλαροπούλου, *Katerína Sakellaropoúlou* [kateˈrina sakelaroˈpulu]; born 30 May 1956) is a Greek judge who has been the [president of Greece](President_of_Greece "President of Greece") since 13 March 2020.[[2]](Katerina_Sakellaropoulou#cite_note-3) She was [elected](2020_Greek_presidential_election "2020 Greek presidential election") by the [Hellenic Parliament](Hellenic_Parliament "Hellenic Parliament") to succeed [Prokopis Pavlopoulos](Prokopis_Pavlopoulos "Prokopis Pavlopoulos") on 22 January 2020. Sakellaropoulou was born in <Thessaloniki>.
